[edit]

  • Rhymes: -ɑleɡo
  • Syllabification(key): ga‧le‧go
  • Hyphenation(key): ga‧le‧go

Noun

[edit]

galego

  1. Galician (language)

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese galego, from Latin gallaecus (“a Galician”), from older callaecus (“a person of a local tribe from NW Iberia”), from a local substrate language; either from Proto-Celtic *kallī- (“wood”) or from a descendant of Proto-Indo-European *kl̥H-ní-s (“hill”), from Proto-Indo-European *kelH-, and a relational suffix *-aekos of Lusitanian or Hispano-Celtic origin.[1]

The geographical name Gallaecia was derived from the ethnonym Gallaeci.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /ɡaˈleɡo/ [ɡɑˈle.ɣ̞ʊ]
  • IPA(key): (standard) /ɡaˈleɡo/ [ɡɑˈle.ɣ̞ʊ]
  • IPA(key): (gheada) /ħaˈleħo/ [ħɑˈle.ħʊ]

 
  • Rhymes: -eɡo
  • Rhymes: -eɡo
  • Rhymes: -eħo

  • Hyphenation: ga‧le‧go

Adjective

[edit]

galego (feminine galega, masculine plural galegos, feminine plural galegas)

  1. Galician (pertaining to Galicia or the Galician language)
    • 1390, José Luis Pensado Tomé, editor, Os Miragres de Santiago, Madrid: CSIC, page 19:
      «Osana ﬁli[o] Dauidi», que quer dizer en lingoajen galego: señor faysnos saluos
      «Osana ﬁli[o] Dauidi», which means in Galician language: señor faysnos salvos [Lord, save us]

Derived terms

[edit]
  • galegada
  • galeguidade
  • galeguismo
  • galeguista
  • galeguizar

Noun

[edit]

galego m (plural galegos, feminine galega, feminine plural galegas)

  1. a person from Galicia, or a person with Galician ancestry
    Nós somos galegos e os galegos sómosche así ― We are Galicians and we Galicians are like that

Noun

[edit]

galego m (uncountable)

  1. the Galician language

Derived terms

[edit]
  • galegofalante

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
galego
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese galego, from Latin Gallaecus,[1][2] from Gallaecia. Cognate with Galician galego and Spanish gallego.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ɡaˈle.ɡu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ɡaˈle.ɡu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ɡaˈle.ɡo/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ɡɐˈle.ɡu/ [ɡɐˈle.ɣu]

  • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
  • Hyphenation: ga‧le‧go

Adjective

[edit]

galego (feminine galega, masculine plural galegos, feminine plural galegas, not comparable)

  1. Galician (pertaining to Galicia or the Galician language)
  2. (Brazil, dialectal) blond

Noun

[edit]

galego m (plural galegos, feminine galega, feminine plural galegas)

  1. Galician person
  2. (uncountable) Galician language
  3. (Alentejo, Algarve, colloquial) someone from Northern Portugal
  4. (Northeast Brazil) blond (a person with fair hair)
  5. (Brazil, dated) a European immigrant to Brazil, more specifically, a Portuguese or Spanish immigrant
    • Jeffrey Lesser, Immigration, Ethnicity, and National Identity in Brazil, 1808 to the Present p. 108,
    • p. 89 referring to Dicionario de Gria, Sao Paulo: Editora Preludio, 1974, p. 62
  6. (Brazil, derogatory) a Portuguese of poor education

References

[edit]
  1. ^ “galego”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  2. ^ “galego”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

[edit]
